ac_results.AC5: FAIL — DOM element exists but drag-and-drop not wired

findings.issue: drag.js is never loaded in the React HTML (HTML_HEAD has only React/ReactDOM/Babel script tags). initEditorDrag() is exported by web/js/drag.js but never called from any useEffect in react_template.tpl. Result: card-candidate elements have draggable=true and data-option-id/data-slot-id attributes but zero event handlers. slot-drop elements have no dragover/drop handlers. window.initEditorDrag is undefined in the browser. window.setEditorSelection exists (React bridge) but can never be triggered. The drag-and-drop core feature of the editor is completely non-functional.
findings.browser_evidence: Playwright evaluate on live port 8770: drag_is_wired=false, card_ondragstart=false, slot_ondrop=false, slot_ondragover=false, window_initEditorDrag_defined=false. HTML_HEAD confirmed: only 3 script tags (React, ReactDOM, Babel). No drag.js src in generated HTML.
findings.recommended_fix: Option A (native React, no external dependency): In react_template.tpl CandidatesSidebar, add onDragStart to .card-candidate div. On each .slot-drop div in KanbanView, add onDragOver={e=>e.preventDefault()} and onDrop={e=>{e.preventDefault();const d=JSON.parse(e.dataTransfer.getData('text/plain'));if(window.setEditorSelection)window.setEditorSelection(d.slotId,d.optionId);}}. Option B (load drag.js): add <script src='/web/js/drag.js' type='module'> to HTML_HEAD and call initEditorDrag() from useEffect gated by EDITOR_MODE.

codex_consult.feedback_summary: Codex verdict: not PASS. Two blockers raised. (1) marginRight:300px narrows main content vs published — 'identical except sidebar' violation. (2) drag.js initEditorDrag never called — functional AC5 fails. Risks 2 (editorDay lookup) and 3 (port 8765) classified OBSERVATION_ONLY by Codex.
codex_consult.feedback_incorporated: Codex blocker 2 (drag not wired) confirmed by QA live browser evaluation and accepted as critical finding. Codex blocker 1 (marginRight:300px) classified as minor/non-blocking by QA: BA spec AC4 tests column widths not scroll viewport width, marginRight is the only correct pattern for position:fixed sidebar, and BA spec M2 prescribes this architecture. marginRight logged as minor observation.

qa.minor_observation: marginRight:300px on main content div makes scroll viewport 885px vs ~1185px in published page. Kanban card widths unchanged (280px). This is the required layout reservation for the position:fixed sidebar — without it content is hidden under the sidebar. BA spec AC4 tests column widths (PASS) not viewport width. Accepted trade-off.

out_of_scope_observations.observation: window.setEditorSelection useEffect has no dependency array — re-runs after every render. Should use [] or [publishedDay.day, editorSession] to avoid unnecessary re-assignments.
